neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case was based on a dying declaration from the victim, who stated that her husband, along with her brother-in-law and his wife, poured kerosene oil on her and set her on fire. The victim also mentioned that her husband had an illicit relationship with his sister-in-law, leading to frequent quarrels and physical abuse. The investigation revealed that the accused brother-in-law and his wife were living separately and were found innocent during the investigation. The victim's daughter, who was eight years old, provided a statement that contradicted the dying declaration, suggesting that the victim's injuries were caused by a falling lamp. The trial court convicted all three accused individuals, but the Supreme Court found that there was no corroborative evidence to support the involvement of the brother-in-law and his wife in the offense. The Supreme Court acquitted the brother-in-law and his wife, while upholding the conviction of the husband.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The Supreme Court accepted the dying declaration of the deceased as a truthful and reliable statement, even though it was not in question-answer form, and held that it may form the sole basis of conviction if subjected to close scrutiny and found to be truthful.

quotes.text: a truthful and reliable dying declaration may form the sole basis of conviction even though it is not corroborated.

witness_credibility.value: The court assessed the credibility of the witnesses, including the eight-year-old daughter of the deceased, with caution, noting that the child's statement was potentially influenced by her living circumstances with the accused and that there was no eye-witness to the incident.

quotes.text: the court has to be on guard against the statement of the deceased being a result of either tutoring, prompting or a product of his imagination.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution established that the deceased was subjected to death at the instance and instigation of the husband, and that the husband poured kerosene oil and lit her on fire. The prosecution relied on the dying declaration and other evidence to establish the case against the husband.

quotes.text: the prosecution has established the case that it was 'M' at whose instance and instigation she was subjected to death by pouring kerosene oil and lit on fire.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the dying declaration was not in question-answer form and lacked corroboration, making it unreliable. They also highlighted the innocence of the accused Prem Kumar Gulati and his wife, noting they were found innocent during the investigation and were living separately.

quotes.text: the dying declaration cannot be relied upon and conviction cannot be based on vague statement.
the accused Prem Kumar Gulati and his wife were found innocent during the investigation and were living separately.

legal_principle_applied.value: A truthful and reliable dying declaration may form the sole basis of conviction even though it is not corroborated, but the reliability of the declaration should be subjected to close scrutiny and the courts must be satisfied that the declaration is truthful.

quotes.text: a truthful and reliable dying declaration may form the sole basis of conviction even though it is not corroborated.
